art: Green-phosphor CRT imagery: monochrome green forms on near-black, glowing edges and soft bloom, faint horizontal scanlines, vector-graphics or ASCII-adjacent construction. One color only — no full-color art, no photographic texture.
mood: A green-phosphor CRT terminal in a dark ops room. Near-black ground with faint horizontal scanlines (the repeating gradient in the background — keep it subtle, never dizzying). Everything is set in monospace, including headings; display text carries a soft phosphor bloom via text-shadow (0 0 8px rgba(74,240,122,.35)) used on headings and key numbers only, never on body text. Signatures to reproduce structurally: (1) section headers styled as shell prompts — a '$ ' or '> ' glyph in --accent before the title; (2) cards and asides drawn as ASCII-adjacent boxes: 1px --rule borders, square corners, no border-radius anywhere; (3) a thin blinking block cursor (CSS steps() animation) at the end of each page's final line. Amber (--num) is the only warm color — spend it like a warning light. The feel: you are reading a live session, not a document. Terse, glowing, nocturnal.
name: Phosphor
tagline: Green-phosphor CRT — scanlines, glow, a blinking cursor
